parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Nicotine is one of the components of tobacco smoke. Nicotine can cross cell surface membranes and enter the bloodstream.
parts.text: Describe the short-term effects of nicotine on the cardiovascular system.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.stem:
Nicotine is absorbed from the blood plasma into the cells of the capillary wall. Scientists have suggested that nicotine is transported from the blood plasma into these cells using a type of co-transporter mechanism.

Fig. 2.2 shows how nicotine may be transported from the blood plasma into a cell.

{{figure:figure_2_2.webp}}

Fig. 2.2

The co-transporter mechanism shown in Fig. 2.2 is different from the co-transporter mechanism that moves sucrose into the cytoplasm of a companion cell in phloem tissue.
parts.text: Outline the similarities **and** differences between the co-transport of nicotine and the co-transport of sucrose.
